tad22fcdd: A refrigerator is the only kitchen appliance that runs 24 hours a day, 365 days a year. It keeps food fresh by continuously pumping heat from inside the cabinet to the outside. Because it never switches off, even a small difference in power consumption adds up to a large difference in annual electricity use.
t4dbd9b71: Understanding how a refrigerator works and what affects its energy use is the first step toward making smarter choices in the kitchen.
t6e83bece: A refrigerator uses a compressor and a refrigerant gas to move heat. The compressor cycles on and off throughout the day. When the inside temperature rises above the set point (usually 3–5 °C), the compressor starts and cools the air back down. A well-maintained refrigerator cycles less often and uses less electricity.
t1c9dec23: Several factors affect how much electricity a refrigerator uses:
t5f57c434: Temperature setting: Every 1 °C below the recommended 4 °C increases energy use by about 5%.
t6547958d: Door openings: Each time the door opens, cold air escapes and the compressor must work harder.
tf274f8e9: Location: Placing a refrigerator next to an oven or in direct sunlight increases energy consumption.
tdd995386: Age and efficiency class: A modern A-rated refrigerator uses about 50% less electricity than a 15-year-old model.
t337a3c8b: A FREEZER works on the same principle but maintains a much colder temperature (–18 °C). Because the temperature difference with the room is larger, a freezer typically uses more energy per litre of storage than a refrigerator.
t4053b175: **A refrigerator uses 150 W when the compressor is running. The compressor runs about 8 hours per day (it cycles on and off).**
tc5455b5b: The electric pump inside a refrigerator that circulates refrigerant and removes heat.
tadd3964b: A sensor that measures temperature and tells the compressor when to start and stop.
t2ed74010: Kilowatt-hour – the unit used on electricity bills. 1 kWh = using 1,000 W for 1 hour.
t2552f972: A label from A (most efficient) to G (least efficient) that helps consumers compare appliances.
t790c4a2f: The small amount of electricity used by electronic displays or lights even when the main function is off.

tb62b5480: The EU Energy Label rates refrigerators from A (most efficient) to G (least efficient). Since March 2021, the scale was rescaled – what used to be A+++ is now roughly class C or D. A genuine class A refrigerator today is extremely efficient.
te17cca54: The label shows the annual energy consumption in kWh. This number is measured under standardised test conditions. Real-world consumption may be 10–30% higher depending on usage habits, ambient temperature, and how often the door is opened.

t9df0e2bf: TOTAL COST OF OWNERSHIP (TCO) for a refrigerator over t years is:
te48ecdb4: TCO(t) = Purchase price + (Annual energy × Tariff × t)

tbb8da705: Annual CO₂ (kg) = Annual energy (kWh) × Emission factor (kgCO₂/kWh)
